title: fix: remap upstream payment failures
author: voodoohop
pr_body_excerpt:
- Maps provider-returned HTTP 402 responses to 502 Bad Gateway.
- Keeps Pollinations wallet and API-key budget failures as HTTP 402.
- Preserves the raw upstream 402 for fallback and observability.
- Adds focused regression coverage.

Root cause: OpenRouter credit exhaustion was being surfaced as a user `PAYMENT_REQUIRED` error even when their Paid Pollen was healthy.

Checks:
- Biome 2.3.10: clean
- Focused Vitest regression: 1 passed
- Full Cloudflare-worker test harness: CI pending

Fixes #13180

gist.headline: The 402 stopped wandering
gist.blurb: An upstream provider ran out of credits and tried to borrow Pollinations’ payment-error costume. We gave it a proper 502 badge instead, while keeping real wallet and API-key budget errors exactly where they belong.
gist.summary: Provider-returned HTTP 402 errors, including OpenRouter credit exhaustion, now map to HTTP 502 Bad Gateway, while Pollinations wallet and API-key budget failures remain HTTP 402 and the original upstream status is retained for fallback and observability.
gist.impact: Healthy Paid Pollen users will no longer receive a misleading PAYMENT_REQUIRED response when an upstream provider has a billing problem; clients can identify it as a temporary upstream failure and retry or fall back.
gist.visual_concept: Depict a cozy API gateway garden where Polli helps sort two nearly identical error parcels: a Pollinations wallet parcel marked 402 stays safely in the hive, while an upstream-provider parcel is redirected onto a clearly marked 502 bridge toward a backup path. The visual metaphor is accurate error routing rather than payment trouble, with a small retro terminal and blooming code-plants signaling observability and fallback.
